method: Paired differences within the same training seed; equal-weight mean and sample SD (ddof=1), not confidence intervals. Query-vs-control uses its own reevaluated control. Query-vs-full compares recorded model AP; adjusted gain differences are also provided to expose tiny control rerun drift.
conclusions: Query-only blur EAA is above its matched augmented control in all three seeds: +0.1392 +/- 0.0914 pp. Full V2 blur EAA is -0.2443 +/- 0.5452 pp versus control.
Query-only minus full V2 blur EAA is +0.3837 +/- 0.4731 pp, positive in two seeds and negative in seed 2. Blur DC is lower than full V2 in all three seeds: -0.3011 +/- 0.0455 pp.
Query-only is below full V2 for occlusion in all seeds: EAA -1.2026 +/- 0.1307 pp and DC -0.9916 +/- 0.5037 pp.
Clean EAA/DC are slightly below own control in all seeds. Query-only is not a uniform replacement for full V2.
Component results suggest an attention-output-gating tradeoff, but do not isolate forward effects from retraining, different active-gate anchor normalization or optimization randomness.

All seeds share the same pretrained initialization and same validation set; this is a three-run fine-tuning study on synthetic corruptions, not proof of real-weather generalization or statistical significance.
next_step: First run frozen-checkpoint interventions on the two attention-output gates, keeping both query gates and all other weights fixed. Use full seed-0 V2; compare learned gates, middle identity, backbone identity and both identity on identical frames. This is an inference diagnostic, not retrained-model performance.
